settings.title: Settings
settings.languageDescription: Translates the app interface AND the content of Libre-authored courses. Third-party books stay in their original language.
settings.changesApplyImmediately: Changes on this tab apply immediately.
settings.startFreshBody: Wipes every course, completion, achievement, streak, and cached progress on this device. Theme, language, and other preferences stay. (Cross-device sync needs a sign-in — without one this only resets the local copy.)
settings.startFreshArmedBody: Tap Confirm within 5 s to wipe every course, completion, achievement, streak, and cached progress on this device. The page will reload with a freshly-seeded library.
settings.signedOutBlurb: Sign in to sync progress, streaks, and lesson history between devices, upload your imported books, and share courses with friends. Libre works fully offline without an account — signing in is purely additive.
settings.generalDescription: About this build, and where to grab the next one.
settings.downloadLanguagesDescription: When you install a translated book, these languages are pre-selected. English is always included. Auto-installed starter books download only these languages too.
settings.autoAdvanceSub: When you pass the tests on a code exercise, jump straight to the next lesson.
settings.updatesDesktopOnly: Updates are only checked from the desktop build.
settings.updateAvailableSub: Libre will restart to download and install it — no reinstall needed.
settings.updateRestartingSub: Libre is relaunching to download and install the update.
settings.updateRestartHint: Restart the app to switch to the new version.
settings.soundsDescription: Sound effects fire on lesson completions, achievement unlocks, streak milestones, and section/book wraps. Every cue is synthesised at runtime — no bundled audio, latency-free, scales smoothly with the volume slider below.
settings.soundEffectsSub: Single switch for every cue. Test buttons still play when this is off.
settings.volumeSub: {percent}% — applies to every cue at the audio-graph master gain.
settings.bronzeUnlockSub: Plays when you earn a bronze-tier achievement.
settings.silverUnlockSub: Plays when you earn a silver-tier achievement.
settings.goldUnlockSub: Plays when you earn a gold-tier achievement.
settings.platinumUnlockSub: Plays when you earn a platinum-tier achievement.
settings.xpEarnedSub: A small pop the moment a lesson flips complete.
settings.levelUpSub: Plays when your XP crosses a level threshold.
settings.sectionCompleteSub: Plays when every lesson in a chapter is done.
settings.bookCompleteSub: Plays when every chapter in a book is done.
settings.dayFlipSub: Quick tick when the streak counter increments.
settings.streakFreezeUsedSub: Plays when a freeze shield saves your streak.
settings.uiTapSub: Soft tick for generic button + tap feedback.
settings.accountDescription: Your Libre cloud account. Lesson progress syncs across devices when signed in; nothing is uploaded otherwise.
settings.signOutSub: Removes the cloud token from this device. Your local courses and progress stay; sign back in any time.
settings.startFreshCloudArmedBody: Tap Confirm within 5 s to wipe every course, completion, achievement, streak, and cached progress on this device, plus the matching cloud rows.
settings.startFreshCloudBody: Wipes every course, completion, achievement, streak, and cached progress on this device, plus the matching cloud rows. Sign-in, theme, and preferences stay.
settings.deleteAccountSub: Permanently deletes your Libre cloud account, all synced progress, and any uploaded courses. Local files on this device are not affected. Cannot be undone.
settings.aiIngestBlurb: Paste an Anthropic API key to enable Claude-powered structuring when you import a book. Without a key, the import falls back to the deterministic splitter (chapter/section breaks only).
settings.copyAnthropic: Copy Anthropic API key to clipboard
settings.copyOpenai: Copy OpenAI API key to clipboard
settings.fableHint: Anthropic's most capable model. ~$10 in / $50 out per 1M tokens. Best reasoning, pedagogy + test design.
settings.sonnetHint: Default. ~$3 in / $15 out per 1M tokens. Great for most books.
settings.opusHint: ~$15 in / $75 out per 1M tokens. ~5× cost, best pedagogy + test design.
settings.haikuHint: ~$1 in / $5 out per 1M tokens. Quick + cheap but weaker structured output.
settings.effortBlurb: How hard Claude thinks per lesson. Higher effort means deeper reasoning and stronger exercises and test design — at more tokens (higher cost, slower). Not used for Haiku.
settings.shortcutsDescription: Click a binding chip to rebind. Standalone keys (Esc, Tab, Arrows) work without a modifier; typeable keys need at least one of ⌘, Ctrl, Shift, or ⌥.
settings.resetAllDisabledHint: All bindings are at their defaults
settings.bindingAria: {action}: currently bound to {combo}. Click to rebind.
settings.bindingAlreadyDefault: This binding is already at its default
settings.appearanceDescription: Pick a theme for the surrounding chrome, then fine-tune the accent, layout, and scale. Your choices persist locally and sync to your other devices when you're signed in.
settings.accentHueDescription: Shift the Noir accent — the buttons, progress sweeps, glows and the aurora all recolour around this hue.
settings.scaleCardDescription: Reshape the whole interface from these dials — every spacing, type size, corner, border, transition and blur is driven by a global token, so one slider moves them all in lockstep. Choices persist locally.
settings.scaleFontSub: Scale all interface text up or down.
settings.scaleSpaceSub: Tighten or loosen padding, gaps and margins everywhere.
settings.scaleRadiusSub: From sharp square corners to softly rounded.
settings.scaleBorderSub: Thickness of outlines, dividers and focus rings.
settings.scaleMotionSub: Transition + animation speed. 0% turns motion off.
settings.scaleBlurSub: Frosted-glass blur strength on panels and overlays.
settings.sidebarClassicBlurb: Familiar chapter accordion with titled lessons and per-chapter progress rings. Best for narrative books with descriptive lesson names.
settings.sidebarGridBlurb: Numbered cell grid per chapter — a 30-lesson chapter fits in five rows. Hover any cell to peek at its lesson title. Best for challenge packs and books with short, sequential lessons.
settings.dataDescription: Pull in new bundled books, inspect cloud-sync state, and check your installed toolchains. Destructive resets live under Settings → Account (Start fresh).
settings.analyticsBody: Help improve Libre by sharing anonymous, cookieless usage data — which features get used and where things break. No personal data, no cross-site tracking. Turn this off anytime.
settings.leaderboardBody: Publish your XP, streak and lessons to the Friends + Global leaderboards (only ever when you're signed in). Turn this off and you still sync your progress across devices — you just won't appear in the rankings.
settings.analyticsFirstRun: Libre shares anonymous, cookieless usage analytics to help improve the app. Turn it off anytime in Settings → Data & storage.
settings.syncLatestCoursesBody: Pulls newly-bundled books into your library and refreshes any existing courses with the latest lessons + drills. Deleted packs stay deleted.
settings.syncDiagsUnavailable: Sync diagnostics aren't available in this build.
settings.accountsDescription: Sign into multiple cloud accounts on this machine — each gets its own fully isolated courses, progress, sandbox projects, achievements, certificates, settings, and cloud session. Switching is instant; no relaunch.
settings.accountsWebNote: Multi-account is a desktop-app feature. The browser version always runs as a single library — sign in to that account directly from the topbar instead.
settings.accountsAddHint: Creates a fresh, isolated library on this machine and opens the sign-in flow — once you finish signing in, this account has its own progress, projects, and cloud sync entirely separate from the others.
settings.accountsRemoveConfirm: Click again to remove — this signs you out and erases this account's local data
settings.accountsSignInBannerBody: This account doesn't have a cloud sign-in yet. Sign in now to bind it; the account is renamed automatically to your cloud display name once it completes.
settings.developerDescription: A floating panel captures every console.log, thrown error, and unhandled promise rejection from the moment the app loads. Useful for debugging boot stalls, slow navigations, and crashes on devices where DevTools isn't reachable.
settings.devConsoleOn: Console panel is visible. Drag the header to move, bottom-right corner to resize, × to close + disable.
settings.devConsoleOff: Hidden. Logs are still being captured in memory — toggle on to see them.
settings.shortcutNeedsModifier: {combo} needs a modifier (⌘, Ctrl, Shift, or ⌥) — try again.
settings.diagnosticsDescription: Read-only probes for bundled assets and user data. If something on the app is missing or broken, the cause usually shows up here as a red row with a remedy hint. Send a screenshot of this pane when filing a bug.
settings.noInstallRecipe: No install recipe shipped for {language}. Try the remedy hint above.
settings.anthropicKeyStorageNote: leaves your machine except in requests to api.anthropic.com.
settings.coverArtBlurb: editorial style so every book in your library shares the same visual language.
settings.assistantBlurb: The in-app chat tutor — a floating orb in the bottom-right that opens a side panel with conversational help. Off by default. Flip the toggle below to enable it; once on, the orb appears and the rest of the configuration applies.
settings.assistantHostBlurb: Hostname or IP of the machine running Ollama. The phone + web build talk straight to it over HTTP on port 11434. A Tailscale tailnet hostname is the recommended setup — encrypted, stable across LAN moves, no public exposure. Desktop ignores this field and uses its own localhost daemon via Tauri IPC.
settings.ollamaHostNote: daemon listens on the tailnet interface, not just localhost. The default macOS Ollama install binds to 127.0.0.1 only — the phone won't reach it without the env override.
settings.scanQrHint: Open Settings → AI on your Mac, tap Show QR for phone, point this camera at it.
settings.hapticsDescription: Tactile feedback timed with what's on screen. On supported devices, every primary interaction fires a subtle buzz so the app feels alive in your hand. Use the cards below to tune which moments buzz, how strongly, and when.
settings.hapticsEnableSub: Master switch — kills every buzz when off.
settings.quietModeOffSub: Off — haptics play at full strength all day.
settings.quietStartSub: When the quiet window begins (24-hour, local time).
settings.quietEndSub: When the window lifts. End-before-start wraps midnight.
settings.telemetryEmptySub: Use the Play buttons above to audition any intent and the count appears here.

settings.themePickerBlurb: Every look is painted from a vintage sci-fi cover — halftone splash and all. Tap one to try it on; you can switch any time in Settings.

setup.title: Set up local AI
setup.blurb: For the in-app AI tutor to run on your machine, we'll need Homebrew and Ollama. Both are optional — Libre still works without them, and you can plug in a cloud API key from Settings → AI instead.
setup.brewDescription: Package manager we use to install Ollama. Opens brew.sh in your browser — paste the one-liner into Terminal, then come back and click "Re-check".
setup.brewDescriptionDone: Homebrew is installed and on your PATH.
setup.ollamaDescription: Runs small AI models locally so your chats and code suggestions stay on your machine. Runs `brew install ollama` (~30-60s), then starts the daemon.
setup.ollamaDescriptionDone: Ollama is installed. You can pick a model from Settings → AI.
setup.ollamaDescriptionNeedsBrew: Install Homebrew first — this button stays disabled until it's on your PATH.

paths.title: Paths
paths.subtitle: Goal-oriented routes through the catalogue. Each path threads courses, language tracks, koans, and drill packs into an order that takes you from zero to a role — entry-level developer, mobile, systems, and more.

rustLocal.title: Compile Rust locally for instant runs
rustLocal.blurb: Rust lessons currently compile on a shared online sandbox — that works with no setup, but every run is a network round-trip (a few seconds, and nothing runs offline). Installing Rust on your machine lets the app compile + run locally instead: instant feedback, fully offline. It's one command, needs no password, and is completely optional — you can keep using the online sandbox.

rustLocal.installedBlurb: Nice — Rust lessons will now compile and run locally. Your next Run is instant and works offline.

import.packCountHint: Split roughly 40% easy, 40% medium, 20% hard across topic buckets (strings, arrays, iterators, concurrency, etc.). Saves incrementally — you can cancel midway and keep what has landed.
import.fixHelp: Copy fix prompt Paste the LLM's reply to a "Copy fix prompt" export. Each fenced JSON block becomes one lesson patch. Patches apply to the installed copy of the course; to ship them in the applying and drop the file into
import.promoteToBundledTooltip: (Dev only) Write the patched course straight to public/starter-courses/<id>.json
import.downloadUpdatedTooltip: Download the updated course.json so you can ship the fixes back into the bundled starter
import.bulkEmptyBlurb: Pick one or more PDFs or EPUBs. We'll auto-detect the title, author, and programming language for each, then queue them up for unattended processing. Failures in one book don't halt the queue — perfect for leaving it running overnight.
import.queueHint: Queue runs one book at a time. A failure is logged and the next book starts automatically.
import.errUrlProtocol: URL must use http:// or https://
import.errUrlInvalid: Not a valid URL setUrlError("Not a valid URL");
import.crawlScopeHint: Crawl is scoped to the same origin + path prefix — directory everything under the URL's "directory" gets visited, nothing above it or on other hosts.
import.languageHint: Sets the runtime for auto-generated exercises. The crawler doesn't inspect code blocks to pick one — you know the site better than our heuristic would.
import.embedImagesHint: Downloads every image referenced on each page and inlines archive is portable. Roughly doubles crawl time for image-heavy sites; recommended.
import.estimateHint: cost less; API-reference pages cost more. Cancel any time.
import.estimateWarnHigh: — above $20. Consider Sonnet or a smaller page cap.
import.bookBlurb: Pick a PDF or EPUB. We'll extract the text, detect the book's title, author, and programming language, and — if you've got an Anthropic key in Settings — let Claude structure it into a real Codecademy-style course with exercises and quizzes.
import.detectFailed: Couldn't auto-detect metadata — fill fields by hand.
import.useAiHint: Requires an Anthropic key in Settings. Runs in the background — a floating panel shows progress and each lesson saves to disk as it's generated, so you can keep using the app and never lose progress on a crash.
import.checkKey: Check your Anthropic key in Settings.
import.useAiLabel: Use Claude to structure into lessons
import.modelHintHaiku: Fastest + cheapest. OK for smaller sites.
import.modelHintOpus: Highest quality. Best for reference docs.
import.modelHintFable: Most powerful. Best pedagogy + test design.
import.pastePlaceholder: Paste the model's JSON reply here. Each ```json { "id": ..., "solution": ..., "tests": ... } ``` block becomes one patch.
import.packModelHintSonnet: Solid baseline. Recommended for bulk packs.
import.packModelHintOpus: Highest quality. Tests are more robust.
import.packModelHintFable: Most powerful. Tests are the most robust.
import.packEstimateHint: Back-of-envelope: {count} challenges × {tokens}k output tokens × {model}. Actual usage will vary.

onboarding.welcomeBlurb: Learn to code through real books and hands-on exercises — all on your own machine. Let's set a few things up; it takes about 20 seconds and everything here is changeable later in Settings.
onboarding.themeStepBlurb: Every theme is painted from a vintage sci-fi cover. Tap one to try it on — the whole app recolours live.
onboarding.privacyBlurb: Libre runs fully offline. Both of these are on by default — flip either off and that data is never shared.
onboarding.analyticsSub: Cookieless, no fingerprinting — just which features get used, so we can improve them. Never your code or lesson content.
onboarding.leaderboardSub: Share your XP, streak and lessons on the Friends + Global boards (only ever when you're signed in). Off means you still sync across devices — you just don't rank.
onboarding.basicsBlurb: Pick your language and dial in a comfortable text size. There's a lot more to tune later in Settings → Appearance.
onboarding.languageSub: Translates Libre-authored courses and the whole interface.
onboarding.learnStepTitle: What do you want to learn?
onboarding.learnStepBlurb: Pick a language and we'll open its guided path — a structured route from the basics to real projects. Not sure yet? Skip it and browse everything in Discover.
onboarding.donePathReady: Your {path} path is ready — hit Start learning to jump straight in.
onboarding.doneThemeReady: The {theme} theme is applied and ready. Open the Library and start your first book — everything here lives in Settings if you want to change it.

ingest.starterAlreadyPasses: Starter code already passes every test — there's nothing for the user to solve. Add TODOs to the starter.

mobile.installUnavailableOnPhone: {action} isn't available from the phone — run it on the Mac that hosts Ollama, then re-probe via the chat panel's retry button.
